findingResolution.reason: Item 13c repairs mandatory headers, boolean/composite spellings, widths, component role/ordinal shape and descriptor consistency, and item 13a establishes reader-only values. K12 still omits the inherited backslash restriction, K6 read-back omits its new census check, and exact-end grammar semantics remain inconsistent.

Phase/ComponentRole are capped at 32 for future registration; PathAnchor is capped at 16. The frozen compact spellings reproduce 646/724 headers within R=768, exact-key field costs, the 1002/1060 example and all 27 initial-event formulas. K12's 13-byte wrapper leaves 243 encoded tail bytes. Field-relative depth is explicit and C-1 uses the same convention. Admission must still reject the invalid read-back strings in SOP2-R3-01.

Cutoff/settle/gate closure/abandonment precede an immutable summary and envelope output; the deadline covers optional logging only; blocked writers are not joined; unconfirmed is added. The lead's post-freeze envelope-write limitation is stated and accepted. Separate state CAS and counter publication still leave a pre-freeze loss absent from the copied summary.

requiredFindings.title: Preserve the complete admitted-kind predicates on read-back

location.section: item 13c header and kind predicates; item 13a; K6/K12; C-4/C-9/C-12

requiredFindings.problem: The explicit wire table still admits values excluded by the inherited types. K12 omits LogicalPath's backslash exclusion, so a decoded value such as a\\..\\b, C:\\private\\name, or an elided tail containing backslashes passes its slash-only component checks. The pinned LogicalPath and IE path law prohibit backslashes. K6's writer now requires the workspace-source census, but its read-back predicate at line 504 lists only lexical checks; a persisted {file:crates/vendor_private.rs,line:1} passes those checks even in the C-9 case explicitly outside the census, and can reach a P0 projection. Finally, requestId and several kind patterns replace the pinned true-end assertions with bare $, without an explicit whole-string-match rule. IE specifically identifies that non-equivalence as accepting a trailing newline in the relevant schema/regexp dialect. The closed reader-only boundary prevents minting authority but does not repair these admission predicates.

evidence.note: A persisted value is checked against item 13c's predicate, and accepted reader-only values are re-encoded/projected.
K6 adds mandatory membership in the owner-controlled workspace-source census to its constructor law.
K6's shared wire/read predicate does not list census membership.
Neither the K12 path nor elided-tail predicate excludes backslash.
LogicalPath excludes backslash, empty, dot, dot-dot and NUL segments.
The logical path law excludes backslashes.
RequestId is restated with a bare $; K9/K10/K14/K15 likewise use bare-$ expressions.
The accepted product identity law deliberately distinguishes bare $ from the true-end assertion, and requires RequestId/ExecutionId to reject trailing LF/CR/space rather than trim.
C-9's lexically valid crates/vendor_private.rs lookalike is explicitly outside the census.

requiredFindings.fix: Make K12's decoded path and elided-tail predicates inherit the admitted LogicalPath backslash exclusion, alongside the existing slash, dot-component, NUL and scalar rules; keep valid names such as ..note and ... accepted. Apply the K6 workspace census requirement to reader-only values as well as writer construction, or explicitly retain an approved release-specific census in the descriptor; reject or reduce nonmember files to external without echoing the rejected name. Use the pinned true-end patterns verbatim, or state and enforce a full-string match with exact decoded lengths for all regex grammars; do not rely on a dialect-dependent bare $. State per-kind encoded V checks at read-back. Extend C-4/C-9/C-12 with backslash path/tail poison, the census lookalike through persisted read-back, and LF/CR/space suffix cases, while retaining the S-OP-1 residual for forged values that really satisfy the complete predicates.

requiredFindings.title: Make terminal disposition accounting part of the freeze protocol

location.section: item 16 disposition/reservation cells, counter copy and freeze; item 17; C-7

requiredFindings.problem: First-transition-wins prevents two terminal dispositions, but the cell CAS and its matrix increment are separate operations in the stated rule. A writer can win pending -> sink-failed and then be paused before incrementing the sink counter. On expiry, step 3 skips that already-terminal cell, step 4 copies a zero counter, and the resumed increment is diverted to the unreported post-freeze tally. A genuinely lost pre-freeze record is absent from the authoritative summary, contradicting overcount, never undercount. Neither the in-flight reservation count nor writer-drained notification closes this race at deadline expiry. The same issue applies to other terminal loss transitions and to global counter updates that begin before the freeze but publish afterwards.

evidence.note: The disposition becomes terminal by CAS; a later attempt sees terminal and does nothing.
Reservation state and the atomic in-flight tally are separate tracked state.
Expiry proceeds even when writers have not drained; step 3 accounts only cells still pending.
Step 4 copies counters; all later counter updates go only to the post-freeze tally.
The law claims overcount, never undercount for admitted units.
This frozen summary is the only source of the loss carrier.
C-7 pauses a producer before enqueue and a writer callback after freeze, but does not pause a loss callback between terminal CAS and counter publication.

Static interleaving: EIO return; successful pending->sink-failed CAS; callback pause; deadline/finalizer sees terminal and skips; frozen sink-failed=0; callback resumes and increments post-freeze tally. No executable concurrency probe or test was run.

requiredFindings.fix: Specify one linearization/ownership rule joining terminal disposition, loss publication and freeze. The frozen summary must include every loss transition already committed before that boundary, even when its callback is paused before updating a matrix. A bounded/helpable accounting protocol or a summary derived from authoritative cells with an explicit counted-state/counter reconciliation can satisfy this; do not wait indefinitely for a paused callback or sink syscall. Include reservations and pre-queue/global dispositions in the same publication/freeze rule, preserve exactly one disposition/count, and route only genuinely post-boundary activity to the post-freeze tally. Base marker unconfirmed on completion not confirmed in observable state at the freeze, rather than requiring proof that the syscall physically has not returned. Add a C-7 pause specifically between terminal CAS and counter publication, with a nonzero loss in the frozen summary and final envelope, plus the corresponding global-update race. Preserve the accepted post-freeze envelope-write limitation.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: C-5 asks for every escape-set character in every K12/K14/K15 value. K14 and K15 now have ASCII name grammars excluding that set, and K12 excludes NUL. Those cases cannot be constructed lawfully. C-4 also says elided tails starting with .. are poisoned, although ..note and ... are valid normal components under the actual predicate.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Split pure rule-E escaper checks from kind admission checks. Valid K12 names exercise allowed controls and escaping; NUL/backslash K12 and invalid K14/K15 inputs must be rejected. Use exactly .. or ../x for escaping-tail negatives and include ..note/... as positives, rather than a blanket starts-with-two-dots rejection.

location.section: field drops, header consistency and projection

nonBlockingObservations.observation: truncated equality and the omitted upper bound are useful, but the text does not state whether consistency is checked over the parsed input before unknown/invalid-field drops or over the surviving reader values. A removed elided field changes the count, and later P2 projection can change it again. The output counters must describe the output fields.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Define the input check point, how an unknown elided field is treated, and recomputation of omitted/truncated after field dropping and projection. Add a two-field round trip with one elided P2 field projected out, plus an unknown/invalid elided field, to show the intended disclosure and whether the whole record or only that field is dropped.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The assertion that both maxima are <=768 does not make raising any cap fail: the human maximum is 724, leaving 44 bytes of slack. For example, a one-byte cap increase would remain within the reserve. The separate fixed 32-byte registration rule does prohibit such a header-table member.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Say cap changes require the applicable contract review and rechecking of the frozen grammar/maxima; increases fail the reserve assertion only when the recomputed maximum exceeds R. Keep the direct 32-byte header-table and 16-byte PathAnchor checks.

location.section: written disposition and closed loss matrix

nonBlockingObservations.observation: Each terminal transition is said to increment exactly one counter, but written is a terminal state and is not one of the eight loss reasons. A successful projection must not create a nonzero loss entry. The text can be read as implying an additional written counter, but it is not declared.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Limit matrix increments to terminal missed-projection states, or define a separate success counter that never enters the loss carrier/marker. Keep the disposition cell for written and its first-transition rule.

nonBlockingResolution.reason: Unexpanded source is authoritative for literal members/templates, reviewed generated output bytes are hash-pinned, and protocol tables must equal the pinned enum. A generator/input pin alone cannot authorize changed output.
The ordered K8 map is now immutable event schema; additions/removals/reordering need a new name, and retired descriptors retain the old exact map. C-2 covers both addition and reorder.
K10's current maximum is corrected to 50, PathAnchor is capped at 16, K8 is nonempty, K13 uses explicit u32 widths/spelling, and field-relative depth is defined.
K6 construction and C-9 now use a build-carried owner-controlled source census, closing the prefix-only writer claim. The same restriction is absent from the item-13c reader predicate (SOP2-R3-01).

The raw bidi example is corrected and invalid K5/K6 inputs have rejection/external controls. C-5 still expects all escaped characters in K14/K15 and NUL in K12, although the new grammars forbid those values; see SOP2-R3-NB-01.
The marker is an elementwise saturating global-plus-sink vector, and the frozen summary retains global/per-sink matrices separately. The 1802-byte marker formula fits that single array.
window and wait limit are configured, since and grace are measured, and force grace starts at stage-1 cancellation. Provider/host CPU and native RSS meanings remain intact.

acceptedLimitations.limitation: The log and frozen summary cannot record the required envelope write's own outcome after the freeze; its result remains visible through the ordinary exit code/output path.
acceptedLimitations.assessment: Accepted. This is not a required finding and does not justify omitting a pre-freeze terminal loss.

acceptedLimitations.limitation: Required-output blocking and kernel teardown are outside the 200/100 ms optional logging finalization bound; already-admitted sink units may complete later and conservative abandonment may overcount.
acceptedLimitations.assessment: Stated honestly; suppression-residual acceptability remains S-OP-7 with X3D assent.

execution.computation: Input digests and encoding arithmetic from scratch scripts in this directory; Python at nice -n 19 with -I -B; private 0700 TMPDIR in this directory.

encodingAssessment.configMaximumNote: Conservative sum of all declared alternative-field bounds, although only one alternative is emitted.
encodingAssessment.depth: Field-relative scalar=0; enclosing object/array adds one; max 2. Root and fields envelope add two fixed containers.

wireAssessment.header: Mandatory/optional members, valid UTC timestamp, integer ranges, component spelling, fixed level and required-identity checks are explicit; complete true-end matching needs SOP2-R3-01.
wireAssessment.identityShapes: The seven listed shapes match the specified owner-created scope model, including Project+Execution without analysis Plan and stored-read Project+Run without the old Execution; no caller/candidate authority is minted.
wireAssessment.kinds: All fifteen kinds have explicit spellings and numeric widths; K12 backslash and K6 census inheritance need SOP2-R3-01.
wireAssessment.readerOnly: Validated records can only be re-encoded/projected and do not mint writer SafeFields, scopes, identities or owner tokens.
wireAssessment.consistency: Nonzero-only counters and descriptor consistency are explicit; input-versus-output counting after field drops/projection merits SOP2-R3-NB-02.
wireAssessment.residual: S-OP-1 owns custody/authenticity; forged predicate-valid records remain possible. The complete predicate must be enforced before that residual is invoked.

controlsAssessment.assessment: Unsafe constructors/impls, scopes/receipt ownership, 33-byte header members, empty K8, max line and field-relative depth are present.
Unexpanded literals, output-byte pins, exact schema enums, caps, frozen maps, maxima/docs and constructor census are covered.
Foreign visitors/formatters stay unvisited and no log logger is installed.
Kinds/header round trips and most poison cases are present; add full inherited predicates, census read-back and exact-end suffixes, and clarify dot-prefix positives and projection counters.
Rule E and wrapper boundaries are specified, but invalid K14/K15/NUL K12 must test rejection or the pure escaper, not legal kind construction.
P2 name matches, zero defects and synthetic guard checks remain distinct.
New timing/output order, stalled marker, reservations and late callback controls cover r2 requests; add terminal-CAS-to-counter and global-update-to-freeze pauses.
Writer census/lookalike case is present; carry the census into read-back and exercise persisted poison.
Environment changes cannot alter effective filters, sink sets, bounds or content with resolver input fixed.
Semantic invariance across logging modes, failure/saturation and concurrency remains.

S-OP-1 custody, S-OP-5 configuration, S-OP-6 public grammar/wording, S-OP-7 crash/suppression residual decision, S-OP-9 consent/custody/member limits, S-OP-10/O4 export, S-OP-12, O7 and O9 remain deferred.
